requirements.heading: "UTF8=ACCEPT" IMAP Capability and UTF-8 in IMAP Quoted-Strings
requirements.text: A client MUST use the "ENABLE" command [RFC5161] with the "UTF8=ACCEPT" option (defined in Section 4 below) to indicate to the server that the client accepts UTF-8 in quoted-strings and supports the "UTF8=ACCEPT" extension.

requirements.heading: "UTF8=ACCEPT" IMAP Capability and UTF-8 in IMAP Quoted-Strings
requirements.text: When this extended quoting mechanism is used by the client, the server MUST reject, with a "BAD" response, any octet sequences with the high bit set that fail to comply with the formal syntax requirements of UTF-8 [RFC3629].

requirements.heading: "UTF8=ACCEPT" IMAP Capability and UTF-8 in IMAP Quoted-Strings
requirements.text: The IMAP server MUST NOT send UTF-8 in quoted-strings to the client unless the client has indicated support for that syntax by using the "ENABLE UTF8=ACCEPT" command.

requirements.heading: "UTF8=ACCEPT" IMAP Capability and UTF-8 in IMAP Quoted-Strings
requirements.text: If the server supports "UTF8=ACCEPT", the client MAY use extended quoted syntax with any IMAP argument that permits a string (including astring and nstring).

requirements.heading: "UTF8=ACCEPT" IMAP Capability and UTF-8 in IMAP Quoted-Strings
requirements.text: All IMAP servers that support "UTF8=ACCEPT" SHOULD accept UTF-8 in mailbox names, and those that also support the Mailbox International Naming Convention described in [RFC3501], Section 5.1.3, MUST accept UTF-8 in mailbox names and convert them to the appropriate internal format.

requirements.heading: "UTF8=ACCEPT" IMAP Capability and UTF-8 in IMAP Quoted-Strings
requirements.text: Mailbox names MUST comply with the Net-Unicode Definition ([RFC5198], Section 2) with the specific exception that they MUST NOT contain control characters (U+0000 - U+001F and U+0080 - U+009F), a delete character (U+007F), a line separator (U+2028), or a paragraph separator (U+2029).

requirements.heading: "UTF8=ACCEPT" IMAP Capability and UTF-8 in IMAP Quoted-Strings
requirements.text: Once an IMAP client has enabled UTF-8 support with the "ENABLE UTF8=ACCEPT" command, it MUST NOT issue a "SEARCH" command that contains a charset specification.

requirements.heading: "UTF8=ACCEPT" IMAP Capability and UTF-8 in IMAP Quoted-Strings
requirements.text: If an IMAP server receives such a "SEARCH" command in that situation, it SHOULD reject the command with a "BAD" response (due to the conflicting charset labels).

requirements.heading: "UTF8=ACCEPT" IMAP Capability and UTF-8 in IMAP Quoted-Strings
requirements.text: For commands with a mandatory charset field, such as SORT and THREAD, servers SHOULD reject charset values other than UTF-8 with a "BAD" response (due to the conflicting charset labels).

requirements.heading: "APPEND" Command
requirements.text: If an IMAP server supports "UTF8=ACCEPT" and the IMAP client has not issued the "ENABLE UTF8=ACCEPT" command, the server MUST reject, with a "NO" response, an "APPEND" command that includes any 8-bit character in message header fields.

requirements.heading: "LOGIN" Command and UTF-8
requirements.text: Whenever a client needs to use UTF-8 usernames or passwords, it MUST use the IMAP "AUTHENTICATE" command, which is already capable of passing UTF-8 usernames and credentials.

requirements.heading: FETCH BODYSTRUCTURE and message/global
requirements.text: When IMAP4rev1 and UTF8=ACCEPT has been enabled, the server MAY treat message/global like message/rfc822 when computing the body structure, but MAY also treat it as described in [RFC3501].

requirements.heading: FETCH BODYSTRUCTURE and message/global
requirements.text: When IMAP4rev2 and UTF8=ACCEPT are in use, the server MUST behave as described in [RFC9051].

requirements.heading: "UTF8=ONLY" Capability
requirements.text: Because these are incompatible changes to IMAP, explicit server announcement and client confirmation are necessary: clients MUST use the "ENABLE UTF8=ACCEPT" command before using this server.

requirements.heading: Dealing with Legacy Clients
requirements.text: Implementations that choose to perform downgrading SHOULD use one of the standardized algorithms provided in [RFC6857] or [RFC6858].

requirements.heading: Dealing with Legacy Clients
requirements.text: Additionally, in order to cope with the case when a server compliant with this extension returns the same UIDVALIDITY to both legacy and "UTF8=ACCEPT"-aware clients, a client upgraded from being non-"UTF8=ACCEPT"-aware MUST discard its cache of messages downloaded from the server.
